This section describes how *OPALX* models the spontaneous decay of
unstable charged particles along the trajectory. Two channels are
currently implemented: charged pion decay
$\pi^\pm \to \mu^\pm + \nu_\mu$ (two-body, [@sec-pion-decay]) and
muon decay $\mu^\pm \to e^\pm + \nu + \bar\nu$ (three-body, polarized,
[@sec-muon-decay]). Both samplers share a common timing kernel
([@sec-decay-timing]) and a common Lorentz boost to the lab frame
([@sec-decay-boost]).

Decay is a *global process*, applied once per tracker step to every
beam that sets `GLOBALPROCESSES={DECAY}`. The input rules are listed in
[Beam Definitions](../../user-guide/beam.qmd#multiple-species-decay-and-spin).

## Place in the time step {#sec-decay-step}

One time step runs in this order:

1. first half drift, field evaluation, first spin half-step;
2. Boris kick, second spin half-step, second half drift;
3. decay of every beam with `DECAY`, in the order of `TRACK.BEAMS`,
   using the tracker time step $\Delta t$;
4. deletion of the decayed parents.

A daughter starts at its parent's position at the end of the step and
takes the parent's time step. It is created on the same MPI rank, in the
beam named by the parent's `DAUGHTERBEAM`. That beam uses the reference
particle and frame of the first beam of its decay chain, so the daughter
needs no change of frame. Daughters are first moved in the next step.
Because beams are handled in `TRACK.BEAMS` order, a muon created by a
pion decay can itself decay in the same step if the muon beam is listed
after the pion beam.

Without `DAUGHTERBEAM`, decayed parents are only removed.

Decays add no column to the `.stat` file and are not written to a loss
file. The beam's particle count drops, and at `--info 2` the log reports
the number of particles deleted by global processes in each step.

## Decay timing: relativistic Markov law {#sec-decay-timing}

For each particle, the per-step decay probability follows the
relativistic Markov law: time dilation extends the rest-frame lifetime
$\tau_0$ to a lab-frame lifetime $\gamma\tau_0$, and the exponential
survival function gives
$$
  p_{\text{decay}}(\Delta t)
  = 1 - \exp\!\big({-\Delta t}\big/{\gamma\,\tau_0}\big),
$$ {#eq-decay-prob}
where $\gamma = \sqrt{1 + |\vec P|^2}$ is computed per-particle from
the stored momentum $\vec P$ in $\beta\gamma$ units. Each step OPALX
draws $u \sim U(0,1)$ and marks the particle for decay if
$u < p_{\text{decay}}$; the parent is then collected into a compact
view (alongside its position, momentum, and, when spin tracking is
active, polarization) before daughters are sampled.

Rest-frame lifetimes used in OPALX (`Physics.h`):

| Species | $\tau_0$ [s] | Source |
|---|---|---|
| $\mu^\pm$ | $2.1969811\times 10^{-6}$ | [@pdgMuon2024] |
| $\pi^\pm$ | $2.6033\times 10^{-8}$ | [@pdgPion2024] |

Note that $\Delta t$ in [@eq-decay-prob] is the *tracker* step in lab
time, not a proper-time interval; the time-dilation factor $\gamma$
performs the conversion. For the small per-step decay probabilities
typical in storage-ring or beamline applications,
$1 - e^{-x} \approx x$, so this reduces to the familiar
$p \approx \Delta t / (\gamma\tau_0)$ — but the exponential form
remains correct for the rare large-$\Delta t$ steps near a stopper or
beam dump.

## Pion decay: $\pi^\pm \to \mu^\pm + \nu_\mu$ {#sec-pion-decay}

### Two-body kinematics

The pion is a pseudoscalar (spin $0$, parity $-$). In the pion rest
frame, energy-momentum conservation in a two-body decay against a
massless neutrino fixes the daughter muon momentum uniquely
[@pdgKinematics2024]:
$$
  p^* = \frac{M_\pi^{\,2} - m_\mu^{\,2}}{2\,M_\pi},
  \qquad
  E^* = \frac{M_\pi^{\,2} + m_\mu^{\,2}}{2\,M_\pi}.
$$ {#eq-pion-twobody}
Numerically, with the PDG masses in `Physics.h`,
$p^* \approx 29.79\;\mathrm{MeV}/c$ and
$E^* \approx 109.78\;\mathrm{MeV}$.

### Isotropic direction

Since the parent pion is spin-$0$, the rest-frame decay direction is
isotropic. OPALX samples
$\cos\theta^* \sim U(-1, 1)$ and $\phi^* \sim U(0, 2\pi)$, then
constructs the rest-frame momentum
$\vec p^{\,*}_\mu = p^*\,(\sin\theta^*\cos\phi^*,
\sin\theta^*\sin\phi^*, \cos\theta^*)$ before boosting.

### V-A polarization of the daughter muon

The decay $\pi \to \mu\,\nu_\mu$ proceeds through the V-A charged
current. In the pion rest frame the neutrino is massless and emerges
with definite helicity ($-$ for $\nu_\mu$, $+$ for $\bar\nu_\mu$);
angular-momentum conservation with the spin-$0$ pion then forces the
muon to carry the *opposite* helicity. The resulting muon polarization
vector in the muon rest frame is therefore
$$
  \vec P_\mu = h\,\hat p^{\,*}_\mu,
  \qquad
  h = \begin{cases}
    +1 & \text{for}\ \pi^- \to \mu^- \\
    -1 & \text{for}\ \pi^+ \to \mu^+
  \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-pion-helicity}
The convention follows the standard accelerator notation in which
positive helicity means $\vec P$ parallel to the daughter momentum.

[@eq-pion-helicity] holds in the muon rest frame reached from the
*pion* rest frame. `Pol` holds the spin in the muon rest frame reached
from the *lab* frame by one pure boost. For a moving pion the two
differ by a rotation, so OPALX transforms the spin as a four-vector.
In the pion rest frame the muon spin four-vector is
$$
  S^{*} = h\,\Big(\frac{p^*}{m_\mu},\;
          \frac{E^*}{m_\mu}\,\hat p^{\,*}_\mu\Big),
$$ {#eq-pion-spin-4vector}
with $p^*, E^*$ in units where $c = 1$. $S^{*}$ is boosted to the lab
frame with the pion velocity $\vec\beta$ ([@eq-lorentz-boost] applied
to $(S^{*0}, \vec S^{\,*})$), which gives $S = (S^0, \vec S)$. The
stored polarization is then
$$
  \vec P_\mu = \vec S - \frac{S^0}{\gamma_\mu + 1}\,\vec u_\mu ,
$$ {#eq-pion-spin-rest}
where $\vec u_\mu$ is the muon lab momentum in $\beta\gamma$ units and
$\gamma_\mu = \sqrt{1 + |\vec u_\mu|^2}$. For a pion at rest this
reduces to $\vec P_\mu = h\,\hat p^{\,*}_\mu$.

## Muon decay: $\mu^\pm \to e^\pm + \nu + \bar\nu$ {#sec-muon-decay}

Muon decay is a three-body weak process. With two unobserved
neutrinos, the daughter electron is described by a non-trivial joint
energy-angle distribution. OPALX uses the V-A Michel distribution
[@pdgMuonDecayParams2024] with the electron mass set to zero in the
spectrum shape and no radiative corrections. The electron mass enters
only through the lower limit $x_{\min}$ below and through the momentum
$|\vec p| = \sqrt{E_e^2 - m_e^2}$. The electron polarization is not
tracked, and the neutrinos are not created.

### Energy marginal: Michel spectrum

Define the reduced electron energy $x = 2\,E_e / m_\mu \in [0, 1]$.
The energy marginal of the differential decay rate is the Michel
spectrum,
$$
  f(x) = 2\,x^2\,(3 - 2x), \qquad x \in [x_{\min}, 1],
$$ {#eq-michel-spectrum}
with the kinematic threshold $x_{\min} = m_e / (m_\mu / 2)
\approx 9.7\times 10^{-3}$. The spectrum peaks at $x = 1$ with
$f_{\max} = 2$. OPALX samples $x$ by rejection against this upper
bound.

### Joint distribution and the V-A asymmetry

For a muon with rest-frame polarization vector $\vec P$, the joint
differential rate factorizes in the standard V-A form
[@pdgMuonDecayParams2024]
$$
  \frac{d\Gamma}{dx\,d\!\cos\theta}
  \;\propto\; f(x)\,\big[\,1 + \alpha(x)\,\cos\theta\,\big],
$$ {#eq-muon-joint}
where $\theta$ is the angle between the electron momentum and
$\hat{\vec P}$ in the muon rest frame, and the asymmetry coefficient is
$$
  \alpha(x) = s\,|\vec P|\;\frac{2x - 1}{3 - 2x},
  \qquad
  s = \begin{cases} +1 & \text{for}\ \mu^+ \\ -1 & \text{for}\ \mu^- \end{cases}
$$ {#eq-muon-asymmetry}
The sign $s$ follows from the V-A coupling: for $\mu^+$ the
high-energy positron is preferentially emitted *along* $\hat{\vec P}$,
while for $\mu^-$ the high-energy electron prefers the opposite
direction. OPALX takes the sign from the parent beam's `CHARGE`.

### Inverse-CDF sampling of $\cos\theta$

The conditional [@eq-muon-joint] is linear in $\cos\theta$, so the
conditional CDF is quadratic and explicitly invertible. Writing
$c \equiv \cos\theta$, the normalized conditional density on
$[-1, 1]$ is
$$
  p(c \mid x, \vec P) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,(1 + \alpha\,c),
$$ {#eq-muon-conditional}
with CDF
$$
  F(c) = \tfrac{1}{2}(c + 1) + \tfrac{\alpha}{4}(c^2 - 1) .
$$ {#eq-muon-cdf}
For $u \sim U(0, 1)$, setting $F(c) = u$ gives the quadratic
$$
  \frac{\alpha}{4}\,c^{2} + \frac{1}{2}\,c
  - \Big(\frac{\alpha}{4} + \frac{1}{2} - u\Big) = 0,
$$ {#eq-muon-cosCDF}
solved analytically and the root in $[-1, 1]$ selected. The degenerate
limit $\alpha \to 0$ (unpolarized muon or zero V-A asymmetry at
$x = \tfrac{1}{2}$) recovers the uniform sampling $c = 2u - 1$, as
expected.

The azimuth $\phi$ around $\hat{\vec P}$ is uniform on $[0, 2\pi)$,
and the rest-frame electron momentum direction in the $\hat{\vec P}$-aligned
local frame is
$(\sin\theta\cos\phi, \sin\theta\sin\phi, \cos\theta)$. A single
rotation taking $\hat z \to \hat{\vec P}$ then realigns this vector
with the Cartesian axes the polarization vector itself is referenced
to (the bunch-frame axes, the same as the momentum's, see the
spin-tracking section); the rotated rest-frame momentum is fed to the Lorentz boost
of the next section.

## Lorentz boost to the lab frame {#sec-decay-boost}

Both decay samplers share the same lab-frame boost. With the parent
momentum stored as $\vec P_{parent}$ in $\beta\gamma$ (dimensionless)
units,
$$
  \gamma = \sqrt{1 + |\vec P_{parent}|^{2}},
  \qquad
  \vec\beta = \frac{\vec P_{parent}}{\gamma},
$$ {#eq-boost-prep}
the spatial part of the daughter four-momentum boosts as
$$
  \vec p_{\,\text{lab}} = \vec p_{\,\text{RF}}
  + \Bigg[
      \frac{(\gamma - 1)\,\vec\beta \cdot \vec p_{\,\text{RF}}}{\beta^{\,2}}
      + \gamma\,E_{\text{RF}}
    \Bigg]\,\vec\beta .
$$ {#eq-lorentz-boost}
The energy $E_{\text{RF}}$ is the daughter rest-frame energy
($E_e = x\,m_\mu/2$ for muon decay, $E^*$ from [@eq-pion-twobody]
for pion decay). At storage, OPALX writes the daughter momentum back
in $\beta\gamma$ units of the *daughter* species mass:
$\vec P_{\,\text{daughter}} = \vec p_{\,\text{lab}} / m_d$, so that
the downstream Boris pusher and T-BMT pusher consume it without unit
conversion.

The polarization of the daughter muon from pion decay is boosted with
the same formula, as described in [@sec-pion-decay]. For muon decay the
daughter electron polarization is not stored, but the muon decay
sampler needs the *parent* polarization, which is read from the muon
container's polarization view at decay time.

## Numerical implementation {#sec-decay-numerics}

The runtime cost of the decay process is dominated by the rejection
sampling of the Michel spectrum; everything else is closed-form.

- **Decay flagging.** OPALX performs a per-particle Bernoulli draw against
  [@eq-decay-prob]. Survivors retain their state, and marked particles
  are compacted into a dense view of $(\vec R, \vec P,
  \Delta t, \vec P_{\text{pol}})$ tuples by a Kokkos parallel scan.
- **Michel $x$.** $x$ is drawn uniformly on $[x_{\min}, 1]$ and
  accepted against $f_{\max} = 2$. Since $\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx = 1$, about
  half of the draws are accepted.
- **Muon $\cos\theta$.** Closed-form root of [@eq-muon-cosCDF] —
  no rejection, no iteration.
- **Pion $\cos\theta$.** A single uniform draw.
- **Daughter momentum.** Stored as
  $\vec P_{\text{daughter}} = \vec p_{\,\text{lab}} / m_d$,
  consistent with the rest of OPALX's $\beta\gamma$ convention.

Random numbers come from one Kokkos `XorShift64_Pool` per decaying
beam, used both to select the decaying particles and to sample the
daughters. Its seed is
$$
  \text{seed} = s_0 + 104729\,(i_{\text{beam}} + 1) + 8191\,(i_{\text{rank}} + 1),
$$
where $s_0$ is `OPTION, SEED`, or $1234567$ when `SEED = -1`, $i_{\text{beam}}$
is the position of the beam in `TRACK.BEAMS` and $i_{\text{rank}}$ is the
MPI rank. Unlike other random draws, `SEED = -1` therefore gives a fixed
seed for decay. The result depends on the number of MPI ranks and on how
the particles are divided among them.

## Validation {#sec-decay-validation}

The samplers are verified by unit tests that compare $10^{4}$–$10^{6}$
generated daughters against the analytic forms above.

- **Pion decay.** [TestPionDecaySpectrum.cpp]({{< meta source-code-url >}}/blob/master/unit_tests/Physics/TestPionDecaySpectrum.cpp)
  checks that every daughter muon has $|\vec p| = p^*$ from
  [@eq-pion-twobody] within machine precision, that the
  rest-frame $\cos\theta$ histogram is statistically uniform on
  $[-1, 1]$ (verifying the spin-$0$ assumption), and that the
  lab-frame energy spectrum after a boost along $\hat z$ is a
  flat box on $[E_-, E_+]$ with endpoints
  $E_\pm = \gamma E^* \pm \beta\gamma\,p^*$.

- **Muon decay.** [TestMuonDecaySpectrum.cpp]({{< meta source-code-url >}}/blob/master/unit_tests/Physics/TestMuonDecaySpectrum.cpp)
  decays $10^5$ fully polarized muons at rest, with $x$ sampled from
  the full Michel spectrum. It compares the daughter $\cos\theta$
  histogram with $\tfrac12(1 + A\,c)$, where $A = s\,|\vec P|/3$ is
  the asymmetry of [@eq-muon-asymmetry] averaged over $x$, and checks
  that the mean $\cos\theta$ has the sign of the muon charge. It runs
  for $\mu^-$ and $\mu^+$.
  [TestMuonDecay.cpp]({{< meta source-code-url >}}/blob/master/unit_tests/Physics/TestMuonDecay.cpp)
  checks the Michel spectrum and its limits.

- **Decay process.** [TestDecay.cpp]({{< meta source-code-url >}}/blob/master/unit_tests/Processes/GlobalProcesses/TestDecay.cpp)
  checks the decay law and its momentum dependence, reproducibility
  with the same seed, removal without a daughter beam, daughter
  position and count, energy conservation for boosted parents, the
  daughter species check, and the pion-daughter spin of
  [@eq-pion-spin-rest].
  [TestDecayChain.cpp]({{< meta source-code-url >}}/blob/master/unit_tests/Track/TestDecayChain.cpp)
  checks how decay chains are resolved from `DAUGHTERBEAM` and that
  invalid settings are rejected.

These tests run as part of the ctest suite.
